start_here: Say to your AI: "Make candidates of my shop opening line, trying lamp wording LEAD L1 or L2 and BEAT B1 or none, one slot at a time, with a claim for each sentence." It runs tool:make-spoken-line-candidates-one-slot-at-a-time.

lists.label: Settings
lists.holds: One row per tool and scope (a person, a film, a piece or the whole account): the settings that tool reads when it runs, as JSON. For this folder the account row holds your own dimensions registry.
alike: a config sheet or settings spreadsheet
a notes page of defaults per project

instructions: 1. Write a request file, for example bakery/vary-request.json: slots (each a name, a base pick and candidates {id: {text, claim}}), sentences (a template with {SLOT} where a slot's words go, plus claim_from: SLOT or a fixed claim), id_prefix, script_path, shot_about, claims_about and out {here, narrator}.

2. Say to your AI: "Make the line candidates from bakery/vary-request.json". It reads the row with tools:list and runs python3 -I tools/fill-a-template-without-changing-its-words/do-work/vary_slots_one_at_a_time.py --request bakery/vary-request.json
3. Read the last line: {"result":{"variants":N,"ids":[...]}}; {"error": ...} says what to change (a picked candidate with words but no claim is refused).
4. Open <here>/lines.txt for every variant line, and each variant's claims file under claims/: that is what a fact check reads before the line is voiced.
5. Keep your own slots and ids in a list:settings row and pass it as settings_record; never write them into the tool's folder.

worked_examples.title: Three variants of an opening line, one slot changed at a time
worked_examples.ask: Make candidates of my shop opening line one slot at a time.
worked_examples.given: From tools/fill-a-template-without-changing-its-words/test/test_vary_slots.py (its made-up sentences) run for real with slots LEAD (base L1 ", with a lamp on the counter"; L2 ", with two lamps") and BEAT (base B1 "It is early."; B2 empty with claim null), sentences "This is Alex Example{LEAD}.", "{BEAT}", "The shop opens at nine.", id_prefix "open-": python3 -I tools/fill-a-template-without-changing-its-words/do-work/vary_slots_one_at_a_time.py --request bakery/vary-request.json
worked_examples.hands_back: Exit 0, prints "3 variants written", then the last line {"result": {"variants": 3, "ids": ["base", "L2", "B2"]}}. lines.txt holds: "This is Alex Example, with a lamp on the counter. It is early. The shop opens at nine." / "This is Alex Example, with two lamps. It is early. The shop opens at nine." / "This is Alex Example, with a lamp on the counter. The shop opens at nine." Variant B2 leaves out the empty sentence, so its claims file holds 2 claims (f-lamp; topics hours, f-hours).

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for tool settings and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and list:settings as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
